title: Big-3 hyperscalers publish AI-services 10-Q revenue footnote by Q1 2027
body: By Q1 2027 the May 7 Mag-7 disclosure cohort tightening — Microsoft's post-earnings analyst-day disclosure of an Azure AI Services run-rate now at $52B annualized (vs $38B prior quarter) with CFO Amy Hood guiding to a Q4 "AI Services" 10-Q footnote breakout starting fiscal Q1-2027, Apple printing services revenue $28.4B (+14% YoY) with Apple Intelligence + Foundry Local cited as margin-accretive, Alphabet announcing $9B incremental capex for the Iowa Gemini training cluster (2026 capex guide $94B), and Meta's Llama 4 Maverick + Behemoth roadmap targeting frontier-cyber parity with Mythos by Q4 2026 — combined with the Cerebras IPO above-range pricing print that puts a public-market multiple under disclosed AI-accelerator revenue, force Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta to publish parallel AI-services revenue 10-Q footnote breakouts inside the same fiscal cycle. The structural force is that once one Mag-7 issuer ships a mid-2-digit-billions AI-segment disclosure with a committed footnote-breakout schedule, sell-side and SEC Corp Fin staff comment letters press the cohort for comparable line items; the AI-capex-vs-AI-revenue ROI question that Mag-7 Q1 prints left unresolved becomes politically untenable to leave to analyst-day commentary alone. The most likely shape is a quantitative AI Services revenue line + segment-level cost-of-revenue + capex-to-AI-services attribution narrative; Alphabet ships first given its $9B incremental Iowa capex needing an ROI denominator, Amazon follows on the AWS Bedrock + Trainium footnote, Meta last given its open-weights commercial model. The bear case is SEC Corp Fin issuing a concept release first and delaying voluntary disclosure beyond Q1 2027; absent that, the cohort lands by fiscal Q1-2027 prints.

reasoning.because: Microsoft May 7 analyst day discloses $52B Azure AI Services run-rate + Q1-2027 footnote commitment.
reasoning.given: Cerebras IPO public-market multiple + unresolved Mag-7 AI-capex-vs-revenue ROI gap pressure cohort.
reasoning.so_that: Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta publish parallel AI-services revenue 10-Q footnote breakouts inside the same fiscal cycle.
reasoning.landing: By Q1 2027; Alphabet first on $9B Iowa capex ROI denominator pressure.
reasoning.plain_language: Microsoft promised to break out its AI sales line in its next big report, so Google, Amazon, and Meta will copy.

summary: Microsoft's May 7 disclosure of $52B annualized Azure AI Services run-rate plus a committed Q1-2027 10-Q footnote breakout, paired with the Cerebras IPO public-market multiple, forces the cohort to follow. By Q1 2027 Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta publish parallel AI-services revenue 10-Q footnotes.
